titulo: Why Should We Teach Children to Code?

corpo:
In recent years, influential people around the world, such as Bill Gates, Mark Zuckerberg, and even American president Barack Obama, have spoken out about the importance of teaching programming to our children. Several institutions focused on this goal are emerging, such as Code Club and Code. Some countries, such as the United States and England, are already including this subject in their curricula. But after all, why is it so important to teach programming to children?

Watch the video

We live in a world dominated by software. Our phones, TVs, and even our refrigerators are already connected to the internet. We can already buy almost everything online, and does anyone remember the last time they bought a map? People no longer buy encyclopedias, after all, it's all on Google. Soon our homes will be controlled by software. Virtual money is already a reality, and we all already know there are cars that don't need drivers.

Demand for information technology professionals keeps increasing, since most everyday objects are no longer merely electrical/mechanical objects and are becoming digital. Many professions based on repetitive processes and simple decisions are being replaced by equipment capable of performing such tasks with greater precision and lower cost than humans. This does not mean that machines will take over the world (not yet), but it does mean that professions are changing, and it is our duty to prepare children for these changes.

In the future, learning computational logic will be as important as reading, writing, and doing math operations. This does not mean that everyone will be a software engineer in the future, or that all professionals will use these skills in their jobs. What matters, however, is learning computational logic, giving individuals the ability to solve problems by combining logic, math, and algorithms.

Computational logic teaches us to break big problems down into smaller, more manageable problems. We can use this way of thinking to model real-world problems, separating out the most relevant aspects so we can solve problems more efficiently, on a smaller scale, and ensure that the solutions to these problems are representative of the real world.

The goals of teaching programming to children go beyond simply preparing them for the job market. Different fields of study, such as engineering, physics, biology, and music, can benefit from the use of computational logic. It is present, for example, in the business world, where large companies need to analyze extremely complex market data and turn it into useful information that will support the company's strategic decision-making processes.

The Third Industrial Revolution is already underway, and we need to be prepared for major changes. The best way to help ensure everyone is prepared may be through education, so it is up to all of us to encourage and promote the teaching of technology to children and young people around the world. We don't have to be mere spectators of technology; we can be its creators.
